central_unknown: Rain is forecast throughout Sunday at Interlagos, with varying intensity predictions. Wet conditions could reshuffle qualifying order, cause DNFs (17 over last 4 seasons), and heavily favor experienced wet-weather drivers like Verstappen — making chip timing and driver selection critical.

budget_tiers.core: Antonelli or Verstappen (captain), Hamilton, Mercedes constructor

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Max Verstappen
captains.reason: Strong narrator consensus: Verstappen won both wet races this season (Singapore, Malaysia) and has won 3 of last 4 races. ZachGP explicitly picks Verstappen as 2x captain for Brazil citing wet-weather dominance. FanAmp calls him 'clear number one.' ML projects 23.8 exp pts (proj 32.1), ppm 1.49, MEDIUM risk, DNF 0.12, pred Q3→P2. ML ranks him #2 behind Antonelli on expected points but narrators unanimously prefer him as captain due to rain upside and wet-weather pedigree. In changeable conditions, his ceiling is enormous.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: ML projects Antonelli as #1 with 27.3 exp pts, proj 38.5 pts, ppm 1.13, MEDIUM risk, DNF 0.12, pred Q1→P1. Topped FP2. ZachGP says if it's dry, Antonelli takes the win. Channels favor Verstappen as captain due to rain but ML ranks Antonelli higher on expected points by 3.5 pts. If the race stays dry or only lightly wet, Antonelli could outscore everyone. Strong differential captain vs the Verstappen-heavy field.

buy.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
buy.note: ZachGP's #1 cheap B-tier pick. Home GP (driver of the day potential), P8 in both FP1 and FP2, budget-increasing asset. Audi looked decent at Interlagos.

buy.name: Nico Hulkenberg
buy.note: FanAmp trusts Hulkenberg in mixed/wet conditions as a veteran pick. However, reliability concern after Freddy Slater's car had issues in FP1 — watch for potential engine penalty. If car is healthy, strong B-tier option.

buy.name: Carlos Sainz
buy.note: FanAmp warming up to Williams duo in wet conditions. ZachGP ranks Sainz highly among B-tier. Consistent points scorer, needs only 2 points for minimum price rise. Veteran presence.

consider.name: Liam Lawson
consider.note: Showed strong pace recently (P7 from back of grid in Mexico post-penalties). Budget growth potential needing ~6 points. Racing Bulls a decent midfield option.

consider.name: Lando Norris
consider.note: ML projects 15.8 exp pts (proj 26.3), pred Q2→P3. McLaren brought biggest upgrade package to Interlagos. Won this race in 2025. Only 4.2% ownership in top 500 — massive differential. FanAmp calls him a huge differential. ZachGP skeptical of McLaren upgrades translating to race pace.

consider.name: Alex Albon
consider.note: FanAmp warming up to Williams duo in wet conditions. Could sneak a price rise. Decent wet-weather driver.

avoid: Rafael Câmara — Debut race in potentially wet conditions in a car he's barely driven. ML gives 8.6 exp pts but with massive CI range [-17.9, 49.0]. All narrators advise staying away. Betting lines flag him for early retirement.
Esteban Ocon — Dropped by Haas, inactive driver. Get him out immediately to avoid -25 penalty.
Rio Hirakawa — Inactive driver. Remove from team immediately.
Lance Stroll — DNF after DNF, budget floor option with no upside.
Valtteri Bottas — Serial DNFs, unreliable asset.
Fernando Alonso — DNF-prone in the Aston Martin, poor recent form.
Franco Colapinto — Penalized in Mexico (P8→P15), Alpine pace not translating to results.
Pierre Gasly — 30-second penalty in Mexico, Alpine keeps shooting themselves in the foot.
Oscar Piastri — ML projects only 15.2 exp pts. Looks lost in the car, gave up FP1 seat. Not justified at 23.0M price.

chips.name: Autopilot
chips.reason: Strong consensus from all narrators. With 4A builds and high DNF risk at Interlagos (17 DNFs over last 4 seasons, rain forecast), autopilot automatically swaps your captain/DRS boost if one driver DNFs — massive swing protection. F1FantasyPolePosition explicitly says 'smoke them if you got them' for autopilot, final fix, or no negative this weekend.

chips.name: No Negative
chips.reason: If you've been saving this chip, Brazil is the payoff. 17 DNFs/DNS over last 4 seasons, wet conditions increase crash/retirement risk. F1FantasyPolePosition says 'your patience will be rewarded' if you held this chip for a rainy weekend.

chips.name: Final Fix
chips.reason: Wet weather could cause a tier-A driver to qualify out of position. Verstappen engine penalty rumors (unconfirmed) add uncertainty. Final fix lets you react after qualifying. Strong consensus to deploy defensive chips at Brazil.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: No narrator consensus to use wildcard here. Better saved for a cleaner race weekend where you can maximize a full team restructure without rain variance eating into returns.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: Rain variance makes limitless risky — you want it on a predictable high-scoring weekend. BoxBoxF1Fantasy showed at Monza that 3x boost can outscore limitless in certain conditions.

chips.name: 3x Captain
chips.reason: If you're confident in Verstappen dominating a wet race (as he did in Singapore and Malaysia), 3x could be enormous. But DNF risk at 12% and rain unpredictability make this a high-variance play. Consider pairing with autopilot for insurance.

watch_items: Verstappen engine penalty rumors — small chance he takes a grid penalty this weekend. ZachGP says unlikely but possible. Would actually make him a stronger fantasy asset due to overtake points.
Hulkenberg car reliability — Freddy Slater's car (Hulk's chassis) had issues in FP1 and didn't run in FP2. Monitor whether Audi takes an engine penalty or fixes the issue before qualifying.

Rain timing on Sunday — Ralpho's weather forecast shows greatest chance of rain in early afternoon, tapering off later. Race start time adjustments possible. Wet qualifying could shuffle the grid dramatically.
McLaren upgrades — biggest package on the grid, components McLaren expects to use on 2027 car. Watch FP3 and qualifying to see if Norris pace from FP1/FP2 translates.
George Russell 5-place grid penalty (ICE change) — not a full power unit swap. Likely qualifies top 5, drops to P8-P10. Makes Mercedes constructor interesting if Russell recovers positions.
Rafael Câmara debut — home race emotion but first time in 2026 car. High DNF risk per betting lines. Avoid as fantasy asset.

Mercedes vs Red Bull constructor battle — Russell's penalty gives him overtake upside that could swing Mercedes ahead of Red Bull. ML projects Mercedes at 64.1 exp pts (#1) vs Red Bull at 44.2 exp pts (#3).
arc: Brazil is the final race of a grueling triple-header and a pivotal moment for chip deployment. The rain threat makes this a defensive chip weekend — autopilot, no negative, and final fix all have strong use cases. After Brazil, the calendar moves to Las Vegas where conditions are dry and predictable, making it a much better candidate for aggressive chips like limitless or 3x captain. Mercedes look set to be the dominant constructor through the end of the season with Antonelli's form, and the Russell engine penalty now (just ICE, 5 places) means they likely avoid a full power unit swap and back-of-grid start at Las Vegas. Budget management is crucial: get inactive drivers (Ocon, Hirakawa) out immediately, lock in budget-rising B-tier assets like Bortoleto and Sainz, and position your team for a strong run through the final 3-4 races.
